subject: Service Availability Alert — Rolling degradation impacting Hosted Inference (us-west-2)
summary: Initial customer-facing alert for rolling degradation in us-west hosted inference, internal coordination, mitigation steps, and final post-incident summary with remediation and credit offer.
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Flynn <sarah.flynn@acme-retail.com>, ops@acme-retail.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Service Availability Alert — Rolling degradation impacting Hosted Inference (us-west-2)

Hi Sarah / Acme ops team,

We’re reporting a rolling degradation affecting a subset of requests served from our us-west-2 hosted inference pool. Symptoms we’re seeing: elevated 5xx rates (~15–25% for affected customers), increased tail latency for streaming responses, and occasional request timeouts. First detection: 2026-10-12T07:52:00Z.

Impact: If you are routing to us-west-2 for inference, you may observe intermittent failures or slower-than-normal responses. We believe this is limited to a subset of hosts in the regional pool and are actively investigating.

Immediate actions we’ve taken:
- Marked affected nodes as draining and started a rolling rollback to the previous runtime build.
- Enabled automatic cross-region fallback policy for eligible customers.
- Opened a high-priority incident and stood up an incident bridge (link below).

What we recommend from your side:
- If you have any critical flows that must remain available, enable cross-region fallback to us-east-1 until we confirm full recovery.
- If you see persistent errors, please share request IDs (x-rdwd-req-id) from logs so we can correlate.

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-10-12-uswest-degradation
Incident bridge: https://bridge.redwood.ai/incident/INF-3198

We’ll provide updates every 20–30 minutes or sooner if there’s a material change. I’ll follow up with a timeline and root cause once available. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your customer flows and are prioritizing resolution.

— Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Flynn <sarah.flynn@acme-retail.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:21:44 -0700
Subject: Re: Service Availability Alert — Rolling degradation impacting Hosted Inference (us-west-2)

Thanks Hannah — we’re seeing a spike in 503s on checkout flows (error rate ~34% over last 7 minutes). Are requests being routed to a degraded variant or is this purely a node-level issue? Can you confirm if AcmeRetail is being moved to cross-region fallback automatically?

-Sarah
VP Product, Acme Retail

On Mon, Oct 12, 2026 at 8:14 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> We’re reporting a rolling degradation affecting a subset of requests served from our us-west-2 hosted inference pool...
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:35:12 -0700
Subject: RE: Service Availability Alert — Initial findings + mitigation

Quick internal update (ops diagnostics):
- Root cause hypothesis: an autoscaler regression caused tight churn on some of the GPU pods; when a pod restarted during large KV cache allocation it occasionally failed to recover leading to elevated errors.
- Scope: ~22% of the us-west-2 serving capacity observed abnormal release/restart cycles between 07:50–08:22 PDT.
- Mitigation already applied: pausing autoscale on affected nodepool, forcing a controlled drain, and rolling back the last runtime build deployed at 07:40.
- Short-term: increased headroom on the load balancer and enabled per-customer fallback routing to us-east-1 for traffic exceeding 250ms or 5xx.

Attachments: incident_timeline-20261012.pdf; query_errors-20261012.csv (sampled request ids).

Next steps I’m requesting from eng (Marcus): confirm full cache warm-up after the rollback and verify KV persistence across restarts. Lauren — please prep a brief status note for Acme once we see error rates back to baseline.

— Ben
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Flynn <sarah.flynn@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:02:40 -0700
Subject: Update: us-west-2 degradation — rolling rollback underway

Hi Sarah — quick update from ops: we’ve initiated a rolling rollback to the prior runtime build and paused autoscaling on the affected pools. Early signals show error rates dropping from ~34% to under 6% for checkout traffic; tail latency is improving but still above normal in a small percentage of requests.

We have not forced Acme traffic to a full cross-region migration — we enabled automatic fallback so high-latency/failed requests will be retried to us-east-1. If you prefer an immediate, full-region failover for all traffic, let me know and we can coordinate a cutover.

We’ll keep you posted and follow up with a full timeline + postmortem within the next 48 hours.

Thanks for the quick signal and the request IDs — that helped us correlate.

— Lauren
Customer Success Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Flynn <sarah.flynn@acme-retail.com>, ops@acme-retail.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident update and next steps — us-west-2 hosted inference degradation (resolved)

Hi Sarah / Acme team,

Final update from our on-call and engineering teams: the incident has been resolved as of 2026-10-12T11:44:00Z. Summary: the rolling rollback and pausing of autoscale cleared the restart loops on affected GPU pods; KV cache warm-up completed and error rates returned to baseline.

Timeline (short):
- 07:50 UTC — abnormal pod restart behavior detected in us-west-2 pool.
- 08:14 UTC — customer-facing alert sent.
- 08:35 UTC — ops confirmed autoscale regression hypothesis and began mitigation.
- 09:00–11:30 UTC — rolling rollback and cache warm-up completed across affected hosts.
- 11:44 UTC — normal error/latency rates observed.

Root cause (preliminary): an autoscaler change deployed earlier in the day caused aggressive scale-downs under specific JVM memory pressure patterns; during pod re-creation a small percentage encountered a race in KV cache initialization that produced transient 5xx responses.

Remediations and next steps:
- Immediate: revert autoscaler change (completed).
- Short-term (1 week): add hardened cache initialization with retry and backoff; add canary gating for autoscaler config changes.
- Long-term (30–60 days): improved observability for per-pod KV warm-up, and a deterministic recovery path that avoids full pod eviction under high cache allocation.

We’ll share the full postmortem (attached) and will propose a goodwill credit for the impacted window; Lauren will follow up on credit/financial reconciliation. If you’d like a technical walk-through of the postmortem, we’re happy to schedule a 30-minute call.

Attachments: postmortem-20261012.pdf
Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-10-12-uswest-degradation
Postmortem ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3198

Apologies again for the disruption and thank you for your patience and fast signal.

— Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
